title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: Student mental health and digitalisation
sections.summary: MOE is asked whether student mental health issues have risen in five years and what it is doing, worsened by digitalisation and learning devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can MOE share whether in the past five years, we see an increasing trend of students having mental health issues and challenges and what is MOE doing to overcome this challenge, which is further exacerbated by our drive towards digitalisation and learning device issuance?

sections.label: Mother Tongue teachers' morale and progression
sections.summary: MOE is asked for an update on morale, career progression and development for this group of teachers, including Mother Tongue teachers, and whether it surveys them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can MOE provide an update on the morale, career progression and developmental opportunities afforded to this category of teachers, including the Mother Tongue teachers and also whether MOE conducts any ground surveys of the morale, engagement scores and aspirations of this group of teachers?

sections.label: Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy Scheme review
sections.summary: MOE is asked to review MCES, which is tied to tuition grants, so PMEs with local first degrees can reskill with a second local degree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In this regard, can MOE review the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy Scheme to encourage mature PMEs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: MCES is tagged to whether a PME is in receipt of a tuition grant for a local degree programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This means that PMEs seeking to obtain a second degree from our local University to enter into a new sector or industry are ineligible for the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy scheme (MCES).

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And that the MCES cannot be separated from the tuition grant is a policy blind spot that impedes PMEs with local first degrees from reskilling with a second local degree to get their foot in a new sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As part of the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), the 23 industry sectors have launched the Skills Framework for each of the sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I strongly urge employers to deep dive into these skills framework, work with our unions, to develop individualised skill maps for their current employees based on the framework for the different sectors and industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: These maps will serve to provide personalised career and training recommendations for every employee and help meet every worker's unique aspiration and needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: How can SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) further outreach and raise the awareness and significance of the skills framework, especially for the PMET jobs and PMETs?

sections.label: Burning Glass on hybrid jobs
sections.summary: Burning Glass Technology analysed close to a billion job postings and resumes in 2019 and reported that good future jobs are hybrid, complex and multi-disciplinary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Burning Glass Technology, a consulting firm that analysed close to a billion job postings and resumes in 2019, reported that good future jobs are "hybrid" jobs – more complex and multi-disciplinary.

sections.label: Khan Academy and local education vision
sections.summary: Sal Khan called for personalised mass-scale education, empowered parents and teachers, and lifelong uplift, while local experts shared a similar vision for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In the United States, Khan Academy's Sal Khan, who was the visionary ahead of his time in creating individualised online student learning free, called out the need to: one, make available personalised and tailored education at a mass scale, citing a list of good quality online resources developed in the US; two, empowering parents and teachers as better partners for education; and three, uplifting every student at every stage of life, including the adults.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Locally last year, education experts such as Dr Varaprasad and Dr S Gopinathan shared a similar vision of a future education for Singapore – one that is tailored to the individual, learning anytime, anywhere and at any age.

sections.label: Reforming a well-established education system
sections.summary: Dr Prasad and Dr Gopinathan concluded transforming Singapore's education system is challenging because it is well-established, facing legacy, structural rigidities and stakeholder resistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Dr Prasad and Dr Gopinathan, both former MOE staff, concluded that it would be challenging to transform Singapore's education system for the very reason that it is so well-established.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They spoke of the difficulties of reforming a well-established and well-polished education system due to legacy and structural rigidities; and how even making incremental changes will require changes across a very vast, complex system and overcoming resistance from many stakeholder groups.

sections.label: Ideal education system clean slate
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOE to conduct a national exercise on what an ideal education system would be starting from a clean slate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But in the face of changes that come so fast and furious, there is merit to consider some disruptive innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I ask MOE to conduct a national exercise to answer the question of, "What would be the ideal education system for Singapore, if we were starting from a clean slate?"

sections.label: PISA 2018 adaptability and failure
sections.summary: PISA 2018 shows Singapore students lag OECD averages in dealing with unusual situations and exceed them in fear of failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The PISA 2018 results indicate two areas of concern for students in Singapore: adaptability to new challenges and the fear of failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Only half of our students said that they could deal with unusual situations compared to an OECD average of more than that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over 70% expressed concern about failure versus the OECD average of just 50%.

sections.label: Desired Outcomes versus KPIs
sections.summary: The Desired Outcomes section in MOE's budget is not totally reflected in the measured key performance indicators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: This is reflected in the "Desired Outcomes" section under MOE's budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: However, this is not totally reflected in the key performance indicators (KPIs) that are measured.

sections.label: Financial support outside mainstream schools
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Minister will consider financial support for those studying outside mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider granting financial support for those studying outside of mainstream schools?

sections.label: Foundation level AL mapping
sections.summary: A perfect Foundation score maps to AL 6 for Secondary 1 posting, while Standard students can get AL 5 at 65%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: In recent years, MOE announced major structural changes to our education system, including the new PSLE scoring system and Full Subject-Based Banding in Secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Primary school, students may take a combination of Standard and Foundation level subjects based on their strengths and choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, many students and parents may not be aware that for the purpose of Secondary 1 posting, even a perfect score at a Foundation level maps to a Standard level's Achievement Level (AL) of only AL 6.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In contrast, students taking Standard level subjects can achieve AL 5 if they score just 65%.

sections.label: Earlier phases and Phase 2C places
sections.summary: More parents are said to register children in earlier phases, leaving fewer places for nearby residents in Phase 2C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Anecdotally, I understand that more parents are registering their children in earlier phases, leaving fewer places for those who live nearby in Phase 2C.

sections.label: Primary 1 Registration Framework review
sections.summary: MOE is urged to review the Primary 1 Registration Framework to help more children get nearby schools in Phase 2C while preserving priority for Phases 2A1 and 2A2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Perhaps it is timely for MOE to review the Primary 1 Registration Framework to see how to enable more children to secure a place in a nearby school, especially in Phase 2C, while bearing in mind the need to still preserve some level of priority for those in Phases 2A1 and 2A2.

sections.label: Teacher and executive staffing changes
sections.summary: From 2011 to 2020, teachers and Allied Educators declined while management executives and management support increased.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: From 2011 to 2020, the number of teachers declined by 16% from 39,412 to 33,001.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Allied Educators, who provide extra support to teachers and schools, also declined by 32% from 1,772 to 1,205.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: However, the number of management executives increased by 260% from 851 to 3,066 and management support increased by 147% from 519 to 1,282.

sections.label: Students per class in 2019
sections.summary: In 2019, it amounted to 33 students per class.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2019, it amounted to 33 students per class.

sections.label: National spending on private tuition
sections.summary: At the national level, $1.4 billion was spent on such additional private tuition.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At the national level, we spent $1.4 billion on such additional private tuition.

sections.label: Teacher ranking transparency and grade quotas
sections.summary: Many say the ranking process is not transparent to all teachers, and removing quotas for C-, D and E grades can make the system fairer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many share that they do not feel the process of ranking has been made transparent to all teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can also make the system more fair by removing the quotas for C-, D and E grades.

sections.label: Teacher performance feedback and appraisal
sections.summary: MOE is asked whether it will strengthen teacher performance feedback processes and consider incorporating this into appraisal linked to performance grade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOE strengthen processes for teachers to seek feedback on their performance?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To further strengthen this process, can MOE consider incorporating this into the appraisal process and specifically linked to performance grade?

sections.label: Tuition fees for students
sections.summary: Most students without scholarships pay full tuition fees, costing $8,000 to $30,000 yearly at local private institutions and an average of $33,000 annually overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Apart from the few who obtain scholarships, most of these students will have to pay full tuition fees for their studies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: This can cost them between $8,000 and $30,000 a year at local private education institutions, which vary considerably in instructional quality and resources and an average of $33,000 annually in overseas universities.

sections.label: Cohort participation rate
sections.summary: The cohort participation rate in local Autonomous Universities last year was 42%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: The cohort participation rate in local Autonomous Universities last year was 42%.

sections.label: Purpose of university education
sections.summary: University education should not be credentialism chasing branded degrees but acquiring market relevant knowledge, life skills and inquisitiveness for lifelong upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The ultimate apex of our education journey is seen as a quest for a university degree with the belief that attaining a pedigree degree from a good university is one of the passports of success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But the fundamental objective of a holistic university education should not be credentialism where students and parents chase after branded degrees, but rather the acquisition or market relevant knowledge, life skills and a keen sense of inquisitiveness that propels one to continuously upgrade and seek new knowledge throughout one's life.

sections.label: Practice-oriented university education model
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a linear four-year tertiary education at 18 still has value, and suggests practice-oriented models with internships, attachments or work stints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: University educators that I have spoken to, on the other hand, often lament that students are unable to grasp concepts that seem so intuitive to those who have work experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, the question I would like to ask is if there are still value in putting our students through a continuous linear four-year tertiary education when they are 18 years old, or should we explore an education system that is more balanced and is a hybrid between a combination of hands-on experience and theoretical knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we should amend and adapt the theory-oriented straight to university model and focus on a more practice-oriented model where we ensure that students should have some practical experience via internships, attachments or work stints before their enrolment to universities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We could also think about implementing a work-and-study model where students alternate between stints of study and work to complement and enhance what they have already picked up in the university and vice versa.

sections.label: Educators spanning corporate and academia
sections.summary: Educators straddling corporate life and academia can complement research-oriented faculties, and MOE is urged to consider contemporising university education; 38,705 babies were born in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Educators who are able to straddle between corporate life and academia as these educators can then complement a largely research-oriented faculties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would thus like to urge MOE to consider the points that I have made above as it takes steps to contemporise university education in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2020 last year, the proverbial stork blessed our little red dot with 38,705 babies.

sections.label: Secondary school completion rate
sections.summary: Each cohort, less than 1% does not complete Secondary school education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Each cohort, less than 1% does not complete Secondary school education.

sections.label: ITE stigma at gatherings
sections.summary: Awkward silences at lunar new year gatherings reflect a mental model ranking university degrees above polytechnic diplomas and ITE certificates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At lunar new year gatherings each year, conversations sometimes crash into awkward silences when parents share about their child’s enrolment into ITE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These silences point to a mental model that has been entrenched in our collective psyche, that there exists a hierarchy: university degrees are more valued than polytechnic diplomas, and diplomas are more valued than ITE certificates.

sections.label: Society fixated on grades
sections.summary: The passage asks why society is fixated on good grades, degrees and white-collared jobs, and says every youth's potential should not be defined narrowly by academic achievements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, why are we, as a society, so fixated on good grades, degrees and white-collared jobs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is high time that we recognise that every youth has potential, and potential should not be defined narrowly in terms of academic achievements.

sections.label: ITE students' worth
sections.summary: The passage states that ITE students might not have done well academically but are not less worthy members of society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While it is true that ITE students might not have done well academically, it does not follow that they are less worthy members of our society.

sections.label: Review of Applied Education
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry for an update of Second Minister Maliki's review of Applied Education to match ITE and Polytechnic graduates' skills to interest and jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, I would like to ask the Ministry for an update of Second Minister Maliki's review of Applied Education to ensure that ITE and Polytechnic graduates' skills are matched to interest and jobs.

sections.label: MOE diploma and mental health plans
sections.summary: The passage asks what MOE is planning for broad-based diploma education resources, flexibility in diploma choice and changing course once, and mental health and wellness resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is MOE planning to ensure that there will be resources to enable broad-based education for our students at the diploma level and would MOE consider to give greater flexibility for students in their choice of diploma and perhaps even allowing them to change course one time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The third question – how is MOE providing for resources to address mental health and wellness issues, which is anticipated to increase?

sections.label: IHL educators and SMEs
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister how IHL educators can support SMEs further upstream in planning for staff reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can Minister share how he sees our IHL educators supporting our SMEs further upstream with the planning for the reskilling of staff?

sections.label: ITE graduates delivery jobs perception
sections.summary: A perception exists that a not insignificant number of ITE graduates find delivery jobs more lucrative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The latter point is particularly pertinent to ITE, where there remains a perception, that a not insignificant number of graduates find it more lucrative to take on delivery jobs.

sections.label: Youth mental health in schools
sections.summary: Rising teen suicides and youth mental health struggles mean mental health education and support must start in schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the number of teen suicides have increased in recent years, and depression and anxiety are emerging increasingly as real struggles amongst our youth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mental health issues often begin during school-age years, especially during and after puberty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Bullying, conflicts amongst friends and social exclusion present themselves in the school environment which is where children spend the most time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It logically follows that mental health education and support must also start in schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Teachers and students often notice small changes in thinking and behaviour in their peers and an individual before a major episode happens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Learning about early warning signs and taking action can help – and may even prevent mental health struggles from worsening into mental illness.

sections.label: Teachers uncomfortable with difficult conversations
sections.summary: Many teachers confided they are uncomfortable handling these difficult conversations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With my own personal interactions with teachers on the ground, however, many have confided that they are uncomfortable in handling these difficult conversations and I quote, "Yes.

sections.label: Teacher training for controversial issues
sections.summary: A CNA article cites teacher constraints and pressures, and asks about training plans and periodic reviews.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a recent CNA article, Ho Li-Ching, President of the Singapore Association for Social Studies Education, found additional pressure present and I quote, "Singapore teachers who wish to address controversial public issues in their classrooms face constraints.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Teachers also face pressures, such as the threat of external challenges or sanctions, and censure from superiors or peers." These uncertainties and fears will undoubtedly lead to some sort of self-censorship and unwillingness of teachers to conduct these conversations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a previous Budget debate in March last year, the Minister had said that with the expansion of the CCE curriculum, every school experience can be a CCE lesson.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, could I ask the Ministry if there are plans to have all teachers trained in such specialised skills and, if so, what is the estimated timeline for this?

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For teachers who are trained, I would also like to suggest for periodic reviews and surveys to be done to find out the perceived confidence versus competence, when handling these conversations.

sections.label: Pastoral and career counselling support
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOE continues to develop pastoral and career counselling support in schools and institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our young people and students would be no different, and I would thus hope that MOE can continue to develop and enhance their pastoral and career counselling support provided to our schools and institutions.

sections.label: Mental wellness and CCE curriculum
sections.summary: Mental wellness and peer support have gained focus, and MOE revised its CCE curriculum for 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mental wellness and peer support have been given more focus in schools over the years and MOE has also updated and revised its Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) curriculum for 2021.

sections.label: Career guidance and counsellors
sections.summary: The speaker says MOE's Education and Career Guidance platform should be extended so every school could have trained career counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will help engage students so that they can make choices that are obviously more informed choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that MOE does provide this support via their Education and Career Guidance (ECG) platform, so it would be good to extend and enhance these resources so that every school perhaps could have its dedicated team of trained, professional career counsellors.

sections.label: Updated CCE and mental well-being
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for Education to share more on the updated CCE and how it supports students' mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister for Education to share more on the updated CCE and how it can support our students' mental well-being?

sections.label: Intervention programmes for school transitions
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for Education how intervention programmes help students transition into Primary and Secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: Can the Minister for Education share more on how intervention programmes today help our students with their transition as they enter Primary school and Secondary school?

sections.label: Equipping students with skills
sections.summary: The passage states that empowering students with skills makes them independent and able to contribute to economy and society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What would be more meaningful is to empower and equip them with as many skills as possible so that they can be as independent as possible and could even contribute towards the economy and society in the future.

sections.label: Special needs children as assets
sections.summary: The passage says viewing children with special needs as assets could maximise their potential and benefit typically developing students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The cost of having to care for them in later years may be greater and this may result in a social burden to families and the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Israel, there have been efforts to train those who are in the autism spectrum for cybersecurity jobs and an artificial intelligence (AI) start-up has found that autistic people are highly suited to their business involving data annotation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: These developments may still be at the nascent stage, but if we choose to view children with special needs as assets to the community, I am sure we will find a way to maximise their potential.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would also argue that beyond benefiting the students with special needs, students who are typically developing also stand to gain a wealth of skills, values and knowledge that are crucial for the diverse workplace of the future.

sections.label: Platforms for cross-interaction in schools
sections.summary: The passage asks whether schools could create platforms for cross-interaction by adapting programmes, redesigning spaces and setting aside time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Thirdly, could schools look at intentionally creating platforms by adapting programmes, redesigning school spaces and setting aside time for cross-interaction during learning and play?

sections.label: SEN students in SPED schools
sections.summary: About 20% of students with SEN attend SPED schools, while 80% attend mainstream schools in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: About 20% of students with SEN attend some 19 Special Education, or SPED, schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The rest, 80%, attend mainstream schools in Singapore.

sections.label: SEN internship challenges
sections.summary: Many students with SEN face challenges in securing internships for authentic work experiences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Many students with SEN find challenges in securing internship opportunities to get the authentic work experiences that they need.

sections.label: Academic scores and eligibility
sections.summary: Eligibility for the next education level often weighs heavily on academic scores, so academic subjects take precedence in curriculum time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Their eligibility for the next level of education often weighs heavily on their academic scores and the academic subjects understandably take precedence during curriculum time.

sections.label: Para-sports pilots and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: Two para-sports pilots were tried, and the passage asks for SkillsFuture Credit usage statistics and a possible top-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Both suggestions have been tried and tested by the Singapore Disability Sports Council through two pilots: The I'mPOSSIBLE programme that attracted over 250 educators to undergo training on the Paralympic movement. and Project ParABLE, a Temasek Foundation-sponsored pilot that offers resources, such as athlete ambassadors and equipment, to bring para-sports experiences to all students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 pandemic has thrown into sharp relief the importance of reskilling and upskilling opportunities for our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Even for those who are still in the midst of their job search, learning new skills through the various courses offered by SkillsFuture has helped them to stay confident and productive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the latest statistics concerning SkillsFuture Credit usage?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can we look forward to another round of SkillsFuture Credit top up?

sections.label: Lean sigma black belt course
sections.summary: The lean sigma black belt course certifies a participant only after showing a $1 million operational improvement to his organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: An example is the lean sigma black belt course, which is an operational excellence training course where a participant receives his certification only after showing a $1 million operational improvement to his organisation.

sections.label: COVID-19 job landscape changes
sections.summary: COVID-19 significantly disrupted the global economy and brought permanent changes to the job landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: COVID-19 brought significant disruption to the global economy and, with it, also permanent changes to the job landscape.

sections.label: Graduate employment survey 2020
sections.summary: A Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey found fewer Singapore graduates secured permanent full-time jobs in 2020, with more part-time and temporary employment during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A trend has been observed in a recent Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It reported that fewer Singapore graduates secured permanent full-time jobs in 2020, along with a spike in part-time and temporary employment, amidst the pandemic.

sections.label: General Assembly immersive courses
sections.summary: General Assembly's immersive courses for technology, data and digital roles typically take 480 hours of live instruction over an intense 12-week period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, the General Assembly's immersive courses that help participants gain skills for jobs in technology, data and other digital roles, typically take 480 hours of live instruction, either online or in a physical classroom, are often delivered over an intense 12-week period.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Queen Bee and Google initiatives
sections.summary: The passage asks how the SkillsFuture Queen Bee programme and Google-type initiatives can be expanded to bring more industry leaders into reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Queen Bee industry leaders, such as IBM and Google can leverage their best practices, cutting-edge know-how and training solutions to level up the skills capability of companies in the network.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Also, the partnership between Goggle, EDB, IMDA and SkillsFuture Singapore for the Skills Ignition SG has the potential to boost jobseekers' employment and employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask: how can SkillsFuture Queen Bee programme and Goggle-type initiatives be expanded to bring more industry leaders onboard the reskilling effort?

sections.label: Pandemic impact on children's learning
sections.summary: Many worry the pandemic will impact a generation of children in studies, skills, job prospects and incomes, though schools mostly stayed open.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Many worry that this will impact a whole generation of children, not just struggling to keep up in their studies, but also finding it difficult later to catch up in their skills, job prospects and incomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We had to close schools and move to full home-based learning for a month during the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But for the most part, we have been able to keep schools open and ensure learning continues seamlessly.

sections.label: Education changes away from grades
sections.summary: Bold changes in the education system aim to move away from over-emphasis on grades and examinations and nurture students who enjoy learning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Most of all, we want them to be curious, to enjoy the learning adventure enough to do this repeatedly throughout life, discovering new wonders each time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why we have been making bold changes in our education system to move away from the over-emphasis on grades and examination results and to nurture a generation of students who enjoy learning and are not bogged down by chasing every last mark.

sections.label: MOE's three priorities
sections.summary: MOE's priorities are equipping students with skills beyond book knowledge, supporting diverse lifelong pathways, and helping students develop to their fullest potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, let me share about three of MOE's priorities over the coming years: first, to equip our students with competencies and skills beyond book knowledge; second, to support learning through multiple diverse pathways and throughout life; third, to uplift our students and ensure they develop to their fullest potential, regardless of starting point.

sections.label: 21st Century Competencies teaching
sections.summary: Skills like communication, teamwork, creativity, curiosity and resilience are called 21st Century Competencies, and teaching of these life skills will be strengthened across the education system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They include skills like effective communication and teamwork, creativity and innovation, curiosity, resilience and grit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We often call these 21st Century Competencies, or 21CCs, and we are committed to strengthening the teaching of such life skills across our education system.

sections.label: Character and Citizenship Education curriculum
sections.summary: A new Character and Citizenship Education curriculum is being progressively rolled out to equip students with competencies to be more future-ready.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In schools, one important approach is through Character and Citizenship Education, or CCE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are progressively rolling out a new curriculum for CCE that will equip our students with the competencies to be more future-ready.

sections.label: HBL and Personal Learning Devices
sections.summary: HBL will be scheduled regularly, with about two days a month in Secondary schools and slightly more for Pre-University, and every Secondary student will own a Personal Learning Device by year-end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, we will schedule HBL as a regular feature of the curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will introduce around two days of HBL a month in Secondary schools, and it can be slightly more for Pre-University.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, it is a meaningful and important part of the curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And every Secondary school student will own a Personal Learning Device – a laptop or tablet – to support Blended Learning by the end of the year.

sections.label: New Centre for CCE
sections.summary: A new Centre for CCE will be established at the National Institute of Education to strengthen educators' skills in CCE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, to strengthen our educators’ skills in CCE, we will establish a new Centre for CCE at the National Institute of Education.

sections.label: New Centre for Teaching and Learning Excellence
sections.summary: A new Centre for Teaching and Learning Excellence will be launched.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, we will launch a new Centre for Teaching and Learning Excellence.

sections.label: Centre for Teaching and Learning Excellence at New Town Primary
sections.summary: A new Centre for Teaching and Learning Excellence will start at New Town Primary School this year to support Primary school teachers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Centre has received good feedback from Secondary school teachers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, to support our Primary school teachers, we will start a new Centre for Teaching and Learning Excellence at New Town Primary School from this year.

sections.label: PSLE scoring system reform
sections.summary: The PSLE scoring system is one major reform being implemented this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: One major reform being implemented this year is our PSLE scoring system.

sections.label: Indicative Achievement Level cut-off points
sections.summary: In the next few months, indicative Achievement Level cut-off points for each school will be provided, simulated from 2020 PSLE results.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, in the next few months, we will provide the indicative Achievement Level cut-off points for each individual school, simulated based on the latest 2020 PSLE results.

sections.label: PSLE changes and Full SBB
sections.summary: PSLE changes are part of a bigger move to provide flexible pathways, and Full SBB has been piloted in 28 schools since last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is only one checkpoint of many throughout one's education journey and the changes to the PSLE are part of a bigger move to provide flexible pathways for learning, and to avoid locking a student into any fixed path in Secondary school and beyond.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are enhancing such porosity in our Secondary schools through another major structural change – and that is Full Subject-Based Banding, or Full SBB.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have been piloting Full SBB in 28 schools since last year.

sections.label: Full SBB rollout schedule
sections.summary: About 30 more schools will join Full SBB next year, with rollout to remaining Secondary schools over 2023 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, about 30 more schools will come on board Full SBB next year, and we will roll out Full SBB to the remaining Secondary schools over 2023 and 2024.

sections.label: Nitec graduates progression rate
sections.summary: Around 30% of Nitec graduates today do not progress to Higher Nitec or other publicly-funded upgrading pathways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Around 30% of Nitec graduates today do not progress to Higher Nitec or other publicly-funded upgrading pathways.

sections.label: University of the Arts status
sections.summary: MOE will grant the LASALLE and NAFA alliance its own degree-awarding powers and University status, making it Singapore's first University of the Arts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because of the quality and standards that both LASALLE and NAFA have achieved, I am happy to share that MOE will grant the alliance its own degree-awarding powers, and also confer it University status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, this will be our first University of the Arts in Singapore.

sections.label: Pro-Tem committee appointment
sections.summary: MOE appointed a Pro-Tem committee chaired by Professor Chan Heng Chee to oversee the implementation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: MOE has appointed a Pro-Tem committee chaired by Professor Chan Heng Chee to oversee the implementation.

sections.label: Periodic review of CPR
sections.summary: The CPR will continue to be reviewed periodically, considering the manpower needs of the economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As suggested by Mr Gerald Giam, we will continue to review the CPR periodically, taking into consideration the manpower needs of the economy.

sections.label: Modular pathways for career transitions
sections.summary: A full-time four-year degree may not best suit mid-career retraining, so modular pathways will be reviewed and enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I appreciate the intent behind this, but a full-time four-year degree programme may not be the best way for a mid-career worker to retrain to enter a new sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will have to review and enhance the various modular pathways to support career transitions, especially into growth sectors.

sections.label: Improvement in pupil-teacher ratio
sections.summary: The PTR improved over the last decade, from about 19 and 16 in 2010 to about 15 and 12 currently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, the PTR has improved, from about 19 and 16 in 2010, for Primary and Secondary school levels, to about 15 and 12 currently.

sections.label: Smaller classes in support programmes
sections.summary: Learning Support Programmes run in class sizes of 8 to 10, and foundation subjects in smaller classes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, our Learning Support Programmes run in class sizes of 8 to 10.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Foundation subjects in upper Primary are taught in smaller classes, between 10 to 20 students in most instances.

sections.label: Investing in teachers and class sizes
sections.summary: MOE will keep investing in teachers, reduce their non-teaching time, and look at smaller class sizes where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we have capable, motivated and a first-rate team of teachers, and we will continue to invest in them and focus their time on what matters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This means continuing to reduce the amount of time teachers spend on lesson, marking, and administrative work, including through the use of technological tools and additional manpower support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And wherever possible, we will certainly look at having smaller class sizes in more areas, especially in subjects where students may benefit from more interaction and more space for discussion.

sections.label: Whole-school approach for disadvantaged students
sections.summary: Schools have piloted a more holistic whole-school approach for disadvantaged students with complex needs beyond academic support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, we are seeing students from disadvantaged backgrounds with complex needs – not just in academic and learning support but also in other areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we have piloted in some schools a more holistic "whole-school" approach.

sections.label: Studying pilot findings for expansion
sections.summary: Findings from the pilot will be studied to consider expanding holistic support to more schools with similar disadvantaged students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This arose from an actual pilot that we have started.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will study the findings from the pilot, and consider how to expand such holistic support to more schools with similar profiles of students who are disadvantaged and vulnerable.

sections.label: 40 places for unconnected children
sections.summary: MOE set aside 40 Primary 1 places for children with no prior school connection, 20 each in Phase 2B and 2C.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the same time, we do not want our Primary schools to become closed circles, which you can only access if your parents or siblings went there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It was for this reason that MOE set aside 40 places for children who have no prior connection with the school in Primary 1 – 20 in Phase 2B and 20 in Phase 2C – with priority given to those who live near the school.

sections.label: Reviewing Phase 2C places
sections.summary: MOE is reviewing the P1 Framework to increase Phase 2C places, balancing competing demands while ensuring quality of every Primary school.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As a result, even with the 20 places set aside for Phase 2C, some children do not get to attend a school near their home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We receive these appeals at the Ministry and we are sympathetic, because there are many good reasons why children should be able to get a place in one of the schools near where they live.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, I agree with Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Shawn Huang that we should try to increase the number of places set aside under Phase 2C.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is the open phase for those who do not enjoy any form of priority admissions, and is, therefore, based on home-school distance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are reviewing the P1 Framework to see how to do this in an appropriate manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Of course, we recognise that any increase in places for Phase 2C would mean greater competition under the earlier phases for the more popular schools We will have to study this carefully and balance the competing demands – to give Singaporean children and their families a better chance at their school of choice, particularly, if it is near their home, while still recognising the merits of providing some priority to certain groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Ultimately, I want to reassure Members that MOE remains committed to ensuring the quality of every Primary school.

sections.label: Student Care Centre in every school
sections.summary: UPLIFT strengthens after-school care, and a Student Care Centre has been set up in every Primary school since last year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: One of UPLIFT's key strategies is to strengthen after-school care and support, especially for those who do not have conducive home environments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: I am pleased to inform Mr Don Wee that we have set up a Student Care Centre, or SCC, in every Primary school since last year.

sections.label: Befrienders trained and matched
sections.summary: About 50 befrienders completed training last December and have recently been matched with families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The first batch of about 50 befrienders completed their training in December last year and have recently been matched with families.

sections.label: UPLIFT Community Pilot expansion
sections.summary: The UPLIFT Community Pilot showed about 80% of 2020 students attending school more regularly, and from February it expanded to more students and Bukit Merah.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The UPLIFT Community Pilot has yielded positive outcomes, with about 80% of the students placed in the pilot in early 2020 attending school more regularly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: As such, from February this year, we have expanded our coverage to include more students, such as students living in rental flats as we work closely with ComLink set up by MSF.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will also extend the UPLIFT Community Pilot into Bukit Merah.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Together with the coverage of students living in rental flats, we are working to support students from about 70 schools who are living in the pilot sites by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This means we will surpass our original target of 300 students supported by the Community Pilot by 2022.

sections.label: Applied education pathways review
sections.summary: An ongoing Review of Opportunities and Pathways in Applied Education is being led to build on progress in preparing graduates.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Ms Janet Ang, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Dr Wan Rizal have also spoken on how our applied education pathways must continue to prepare our graduates for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have made significant progress over the past few years and I am leading an ongoing Review of Opportunities and Pathways in Applied Education to build on this foundation.

sections.label: ITE curricular structure enhancement
sections.summary: The review's first moves include enhancing ITE's curricular structure, with over half of 2019 Nitec graduates progressing immediately to Higher Nitec.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: One of the first moves we will undertake in this review is to enhance the ITE's curricular structure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: More than half of the 2019 cohort of Nitec graduates progressed immediately to a Higher Nitec, up from just under half the year before.

sections.label: Streamlining ITE curriculum
sections.summary: ITE will make structural changes and streamline its curriculum so more students can attain a Higher Nitec in a shorter duration.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To this end, we will make some structural changes in ITE.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We want all ITE students to aspire to attain their Higher Nitec qualification when they enrol in ITE.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Today, ITE offers both Nitec and Higher Nitec courses, with the Higher Nitec building on the foundation established during Nitec.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will streamline the ITE curriculum to provide more students the opportunity to attain a Higher Nitec in a shorter duration.

sections.label: CEP expansion in Polytechnics
sections.summary: From 2023, CEPs will be introduced in Arts, Design and Media, and Sciences clusters in all Polytechnics, with 25% of Year 1 students expected to enter via a CEP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Out of the 2019 cohort of CEP students, 90% agreed that their CEP has helped them discover their interest and aptitude.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Building on this, we will introduce CEPs in the Arts, Design and Media, and Sciences clusters in all Polytechnics from 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: With this change, we expect 25% of Year 1 diploma students to enter Polytechnic via a CEP, up from 20% currently.

sections.label: UPLIFT expansion and post-secondary routes
sections.summary: The UPLIFT Community Pilot Programme is expanded, including into Bukit Merah, while almost 70% of each post-secondary cohort choose the Polytechnic and ITE route.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: One key change is the expansion of the UPLIFT Community Pilot Programme, including extending it into Bukit Merah estate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Today, at the post-secondary level, almost 70% of each cohort choose the Polytechnic and ITE route.

sections.label: Streamlining ITE curriculum
sections.summary: The ITE curriculum will be streamlined so more students can attain Higher Nitec in a shorter duration.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To this end, we will streamline the ITE curriculum to provide more students with the opportunity to attain Higher Nitec within a shorter duration.

sections.label: Malay intake in STEM
sections.summary: Over half the Malay intake in Institutes of Higher Learning are taking STEM courses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Today, we find that over half the Malay intake in our Institutes of Higher Learning are taking STEM courses.

sections.label: Perkasa Warisan camp reach
sections.summary: Since its 2018 introduction, the Perkasa Warisan camp has reached over 1,400 students across 39 primary and secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Since we introduced it in 2018, the Perkasa Warisan camp has reached out to over 1,400 students across 39 primary and secondary schools.

sections.label: Refreshed CCE curriculum
sections.summary: The refreshed Character and Citizenship Education curriculum has been implemented, starting with Secondary schools this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As Minister Wong has shared, we have been implementing the refreshed Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) curriculum, starting with Secondary schools this year.

sections.label: New Centre for CCE
sections.summary: A new Centre for CCE will be launched at NIE by end 2022 to helm teacher education for CCE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Ms Carrie Tan and Dr Shahira Abdullah have also asked how teachers are equipped to strengthen mental health support and navigate contemporary issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will be launching a new "Centre for CCE" at NIE to helm teacher education for CCE by end 2022.

sections.label: Specialised CCE teachers
sections.summary: From 2022 onwards, every pre-University institution will be equipped with specialised CCE teachers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: From 2022 onwards, every pre-University institution will also be equipped with specialised CCE teachers.

sections.label: Peer support in schools
sections.summary: MOE announced that a peer support culture and structure will be established in every school by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Another key pillar of mental health support is peer support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Hence, as MOE has announced last year, we will establish a peer support culture and structure in every school by the end of this year.

sections.label: Youth Mental Well-Being Network
sections.summary: Last year, MSF, MOH and MOE started the Youth Mental Well-Being (YMWB) Network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Last year, MSF, MOH and MOE started the Youth Mental Well-Being (YMWB) Network.

sections.label: TRANSIT for P1 students
sections.summary: MOE is introducing TRANSIT, a targeted intervention, to all Primary schools by 2026 for P1 students with social and behavioural needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MOE is, therefore, introducing a new targeted intervention, called TRANSIT (or TRANsition Support for InTegration), to all Primary schools by 2026 for P1 students with social and behavioural needs.

sections.label: TRANSIT pilot and rollout
sections.summary: By end 2021 MOE would have piloted TRANSIT in about 40 schools, and will roll it out in all Primary schools by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: By end 2021, MOE would have piloted TRANSIT in about 40 schools – or one out of five Primary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As the pilot outcomes have been promising, MOE will roll out TRANSIT in all Primary schools by 2026, benefiting around five to 10 P1 students in each school per year.

sections.label: SPED graduates' outcomes
sections.summary: About half of SPED graduates are successfully employed or progress to post-Secondary educational institutions like ITE and other further training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Overall, about half of SPED graduates are successfully employed or progress to post-Secondary educational institutions like ITE and other further training.

sections.label: GOS expansion to 600 students
sections.summary: With the expansion, GOS will cater to 600 students aged seven to 18, from 450 today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With the expansion, GOS will cater to 600 students aged seven to 18, from 450 today.

sections.label: CCE centre and TRANSIT programmes
sections.summary: A new Centre for CCE is launched to enhance professional development and pedagogies, with new programmes like TRANSIT for Primary 1 students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):    In a rapidly changing world, having the resilience and perseverance to surmount challenges is critical, hence, we need to place more focus on the character development and education of students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are thus launching a new Centre for CCE to enhance professional development for CCE and also develop pedagogies which will best help our students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We also recognise that CCE has to be founded on values, and this requires schools,Mother Tongue teachers, families and the community to work closely together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are also rolling out new programmes such as TRANSIT which will benefit Primary 1 students with behavioural and social issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Such targeted interventions during an important phase, when our children have just embarked on their primary education, can help ensure that they can better adapt to their schooling environment.

sections.label: Extended wage support for graduates
sections.summary: The measure is extended to 31 March 2022, with companies receiving 45% wage support on top of Jobs Growth Incentive support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To support more students who are graduating this year, we will extend this measure to 31 March 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The companies will receive wage support of 45%, on top of the wage support under the Jobs Growth Incentive.

sections.label: SGUnited programmes extended
sections.summary: Close to 10,000 trainees enrolled in SGUnited Skills and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways – Company Training programmes, which will be extended to 31 March 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Altogether, close to 10,000 other trainees have enrolled in SGUnited Skills and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways – Company Training programmes, with the first courses having just completed in February.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Skills and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways – Company Training programmes will be extended by an additional year to 31 March 2022.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Queen Bees and enterprises
sections.summary: 22 SkillsFuture Queen Bees have been onboarded and more than 400 enterprises, mostly SMEs, supported.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We continue to help employers invest in the skills development of their workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We have onboarded 22 SkillsFuture Queen Bees and supported more than 400 enterprises, most of which are SMEs.

sections.label: NACE and SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit
sections.summary: NACE, established in 2018, has supported about 530 companies, and about 3,400 eligible employers have sent workers for SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit-supportable training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: NACE was established in 2018 to strengthen the capabilities of companies to deliver training at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Thus far, NACE has supported about 530 companies in building workplace-based learning capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To support employers in pursuing enterprise and workforce transformation, we launched the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: So far, about 3,400 eligible employers have sent their workers for SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit-supportable training programmes.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit usage increase
sections.summary: More than 188,000 Singaporeans utilised their SkillsFuture Credit in 2020, up from about 156,000 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: More than 188,000 Singaporeans utilised their SkillsFuture Credit in 2020, up from about 156,000 Singaporeans in 2019.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Qualification Award phase-out
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Qualification Award, tied to full qualifications, will be phased out from 1 January 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Lastly, in line with the SkillsFuture message for individuals to pursue their own training pathway and take up industry-relevant modular courses, we will phase out the SkillsFuture Qualification Award which is tied to completion of full qualifications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will implement these changes from 1 January 2022 onwards.

sections.label: Questions on SPED and inclusion
sections.summary: The Member asks why students with mild intellectual disability cannot join mainstream schools and requests joint visioning and lifelong learning SPED pilots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: One is, why would students with mild intellectual disability (ID) with no other conditions, why cannot they be included into mainstream schools, for example?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Two, can the Minister of State comment on my request for joint visioning for SPED schools of the future?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: And also, to ask whether MOE would consider looking into piloting lifelong learning SPED schools which might improve the landscape and the outcomes for students with SEN needs in SPED schools.

sections.label: Special needs students in mainstream schools
sections.summary: Currently, 80% of students with special needs are already in mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Currently, 80% of our students with special needs are already in mainstream schools.

sections.label: SEN support officers for ITE
sections.summary: In 2019, ITE received an additional six SEN support officers, bringing the number to 19 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Given that we are also having more SEN students in ITE, we have also been increasing resources to support SEN students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: For example, in 2019, we provided ITE with an additional six SEN support officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We have added six to augment the resources that ITE had as well as supporting the SEN support office.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: This brings the number to 19 in 2020.

sections.label: ITE social emotional counsellors

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Today, ITE has 19 social emotional counsellors across the three colleges.

sections.label: Teacher appraisal system discussion
sections.summary: The Member says he previously discussed the appraisal system with Mr Louis Ng and explained that teachers have an appraisal system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, we have had this discussion with the Member Mr Louis Ng before, where he filed some questions on the appraisal system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I have explained that we do have an appraisal system for our teachers.

sections.label: Teacher appraisal system review
sections.summary: The performance management system supports teachers and will be reviewed with the Civil Service, including possible punitive consequences of lower grades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The performance management system we have in place supports this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will continue to review how the appraisal system can be more effective and can be more supportive of our teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The system is aligned with the rest of the Civil Service, so we will have to do this together with the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But where it comes to some of what Mr Ng talked about – punitive consequences of getting a lower performance grade – that is certainly something that MOE can look at.
